question: If the first-pitch outcome draw of the registered planning Q estimator (samples 6, pitch cap 12, CRN across candidate actions) is replaced by its exact expectation over the 10 outcome classes (Rao-Blackwellized first step, RB), is the G0 P3 tau 0.1 law stable between two independent planning seeds, at a per-decision cost of at most 4x the registered planner?
operational_definition_of_stable: On the registered decision set, the P3 laws of the same planner computed with planning seeds 0 and 5 have top-1 (argmax of the law) agreement whose whole-game bootstrap 95% lower bound is >= 0.95 AND mean total variation 0.5*sum|pi_0 - pi_5| whose 95% upper bound is <= 0.02. Cost = conditional rows per decision relative to the registered planner.

hypotheses.H2_secondary_descriptive: RB6 top-1 agreement exceeds A0 (paired gain 95% lower bound > 0). Empirical only: Rao-Blackwell keeps the expectation of each Q(a) and of each Q contrast and lowers their variance, but does not guarantee better argmax agreement (a nonlinear statistic) or a positive finite-sample bound; a negative or inconclusive H2 is reported as is and never suppresses or invalidates the registered result
hypotheses.H3: RB6 is more efficient than brute-force sampling (VRF / r_rows > 1)
hypotheses.H4_descriptive: residual disagreement concentrates in small effective-gap bins (near ties; policy churn)
hypotheses.H5_descriptive: lower search noise lowers the mean KL(law || reference) (noise-induced deviation; optimizer's curse)
hypotheses.H6_optional_descriptive: frozen-history DP-vs-RB law agreement is reported next to RB-vs-RB agreement; no ordering between them is claimed (DP is a different estimand)

arms.estimator: RaoBlackwellFirstStep: Q_RB(a) = (1/S) sum_i sum_o p(o | s0, a, d_i(a)) * W_i(a, o); d_i(a) = pool(s0, a)[floor(U_i[0,1]*400)] as in the registered planner; W = terminal WE for terminal outcomes, else the value of a BC rollout from the child state (count update, history + (a, d_i, o)) using U_i[1:, :], shared by every candidate action and every outcome child (CRN); pitch cap 12 in total (first pitch + 11), same cutoff
arms.property: with the same seed, RB6 is the conditional expectation of A0 given the delivery uniforms and the continuation uniforms: same expectation (incl. truncation), variance of each Q(a) and of every difference Q(a)-Q(a') not larger (Rao-Blackwell)

what_the_approximation_changes: after the first pitch the predictor does not see simulated pitches (sequencing effects dropped; the root pitch is exact)
no pitch cap and no cutoff (two-strike foul loops solved exactly)
therefore a different estimand: judged by fidelity to RB and by cost, never by seed stability (trivially 1)
arms.games: FH-DP subsample (10 games, about 2,500 decisions derived from 250.4 decisions per game)
arms.rows_per_decision: n * (400 + (C - 1) * 40), C = reachable counts (12 at 0-0); e.g. 4,200 rows for n = 5 at 0-0 versus about 94 for one A0 call (arithmetic)

excluded: member-level Q averaging (plan with each of the five G0 members and average Q): G0 already plans with the member-mean prediction, so this is a different estimand (Jensen gap) at 5x cost and no remedy for seed noise; member spread is left to track C1
Rao-Blackwellizing the second pitch as well: children multiply again by up to 3, no basis to stay within the 4x cost rule

seeds.crn: per decision and seed k: key = planning_seed(state, support, k); U = default_rng(key).random((S, 12, 3)), shared by every candidate action. A0 and RB use the same U: delivery index U[i,0,1] shared; outcome U[i,0,2] used by A0 only (integrated by RB); continuation U[i,1:,:] shared by the A0 drawn child and all RB children. For one seed, samples 6/12/48 share their first 6 samples (C-order fill). FH-DP has no seed.
seeds.determinism: Q depends only on (seed, state, support), so results do not depend on order; a fresh RB seed-0 planner must reproduce 200 decisions at atol 0.0

primary: top-1 agreement between the seed-0 and seed-5 P3 laws of an arm (argmax of the law)
mean TV between those laws, with quantiles 0.5/0.9/0.99/1.0 and share TV > 0.05
r_rows(X) = sum of conditional rows of arm X / sum of conditional rows of A0 for the same seed, averaged over the two seeds
secondary_descriptive: agreement and mean TV by effective-gap bin; g_eff = tau*log(pi_R[j1]/pi_R[j2]) = (Q_R[j1]-Q_R[j2]) + tau*log(BC[j1]/BC[j2]) for the top-2 actions of the REF-RB6 law, and by raw Q gap g_Q; bins in WE [0,0.0025), [0.0025,0.005), [0.005,0.01), [0.01,0.02), [0.02,0.05), [0.05,inf); |M| = 1 reported separately; the same bins for A0, RB6, STAB-01 K3/K5 columns and optional arms
mean KL(law || masked reference) per arm (mean of the two seeds) and the paired difference to A0

VRF = sum_d v_A0(d) / sum_d v_RB6(d) with v_X = sum_{a != a*} Var_i[Y_i(a) - Y_i(a*)] / S, a* = top-1 of the REF-RB6 law, seed-5 pair; efficiency = VRF / r_rows (Q-contrast variance per row versus brute force under variance ~ 1/S; not an agreement claim)

paired top-1 agreement gain RB6 minus STAB-01 K_c, K_c = cheapest measured K in {3, 5} with K >= r_rows, i.e. a measured point not cheaper than RB6, not an equal-cost comparator (none if r_rows > 5, unless BF48 ran and 8 >= r_rows)
mean max |Q_0 - Q_5| on the support; paired-difference SE and the D-9 noise ratio (max SE / tau) quantiles

RB residual: per-decision median of (variance of the terminal-outcome term, which moves only with the first-pitch delivery draw) / (RB sample variance), a descriptive ratio, not an additive share (the covariance with the continuation term is reported next to it); cap-12 truncation share per arm
planner wall time per decision per arm and seed (time.perf_counter), total seconds, peak RSS

FH-DP (if run): law agreement and TV versus RB seeds 0/5/100, and RB-RB agreement on the same decisions, side by side with their paired difference (descriptive; no ordering implied); rows and ms per decision

intervals.paired: paired differences use the same draws
intervals.subsamples_and_confirmation: BF48, FH-DP and the confirmation slice each use their own draw table over their own games (data.subsamples.bootstrap, data.confirmation_slice.bootstrap)
intervals.empty_denominator: a replicate with zero decisions in a bin or stratum leaves that ratio undefined (NaN); intervals use the valid replicates and report their count; a bin empty in the original sample is reported as none

metrics.not_measured: policy value, OPE, recommendation quality (no reward, WE result, events kind or next-row state is read; outcomes_read false)

stable.rule: STABLE_X iff top-1 agreement 95% lower bound >= 0.95 AND mean TV 95% upper bound <= 0.02

verdict.precedence: (0) smoke r_b > 4.0 -> COST_EXCEEDED_AT_SMOKE; (1) some run arm is STABLE and COST_OK -> STABLE_WITHIN_COST:<cheapest such arm>; (2) else some run arm is STABLE -> STABLE_OVER_COST:<that arm> (at least one STABLE arm and no arm both STABLE and COST_OK); (3) else NOT_STABLE
verdict.COST_EXCEEDED_AT_SMOKE: pre-run stop: smoke r_b > 4.0; the full run is not started (the smoke computes no comparison)
verdict.STABLE_WITHIN_COST: some run arm X in {RB6, RB12 if run} with STABLE_X and COST_OK_X; the cheapest such X
verdict.STABLE_OVER_COST: at least one run arm STABLE and no run arm both STABLE and COST_OK
verdict.NOT_STABLE: no run arm STABLE (incl. an aborted pass C: flag RB12_ABORTED)
partition: RB6 STABLE and COST_OK -> STABLE_WITHIN_COST:RB6 (RB12 not run)
RB6 STABLE and not COST_OK -> STABLE_OVER_COST:RB6 (RB12 not run)
RB6 not STABLE, smoke r_b > 2.0 (RB12 not run) -> NOT_STABLE
RB6 not STABLE, RB12 run, RB12 STABLE and COST_OK -> STABLE_WITHIN_COST:RB12
RB6 not STABLE, RB12 run, RB12 STABLE and not COST_OK -> STABLE_OVER_COST:RB12 (whatever RB6's COST_OK)
RB6 not STABLE, RB12 run, RB12 not STABLE -> NOT_STABLE
RB6 not STABLE, RB12 condition met but pass C aborted -> NOT_STABLE with flag RB12_ABORTED
pass M aborted -> no verdict label (aborted.json, nothing citable)
verdict.exclusivity: RB12 runs only when RB6 is not STABLE, so at most one arm can be STABLE; the rows above are exhaustive and mutually exclusive

secondary_flags_no_verdict_effect.rb_improves_over_baseline: RB6 minus A0 paired top-1 gain 95% lower bound > 0 (H2, descriptive)
secondary_flags_no_verdict_effect.rb_beats_measured_bruteforce: RB6 minus STAB-01 K_c paired top-1 gain 95% lower bound > 0 (K_c is the cheapest measured K not cheaper than RB6; not an equal-cost comparison)

decision_rules.approval: 0.95, 0.02 and 4.0 approved by Song exactly as drafted (D186 4-①, docs/decisions.md:325); fixed before any result is read; they remain judgement values in origin

judgement_values.0.95: the D153 service criterion (live vs final top-1 agreement >= 95%, docs/decisions.md:254), reused exactly as in EXP-STAB-01 for direct comparability; no measured basis for the planner
judgement_values.0.02: below the EXP-STAB-01 K5 mean TV 0.0230 [0.0216, 0.0244] (i.e. better than 5x brute force) and 0.62x the G0->G15 predictor-swap TV 0.0323, so a predictor change of that size would stand above the search noise; read on the upper bound, the same conservative direction as the agreement lower bound
judgement_values.4.0: 4x brute force equals K=4 seed averaging; the measured K5 (5x) still had lower bound 0.9419, so passing within 4x means meeting, at a cost below K5, thresholds that none of the measured points (K = 1, 3, 5) met; K4 was not measured, so no claim that the arm is cheaper than unmeasured alternatives or that K4 must fail; about 0.13 s per decision on the Mac mini (derived from STAB-01 33 ms per planner call), below 1% of the measured pitch-to-first-receipt latency median 21.0 s (D181, docs/decisions.md:315; the service-path planner latency itself is not measured)

pass M only: A0 per-decision K1_tv and K1_top1_same equal the STAB-01 columns (never in the smoke or another pass; exact equality expected: same code path and batches); stop if fewer than 99.9% of decisions match (judgement value: allowance for environment-level float nondeterminism)

pass M (RB6, all 6 samples) and pass C (RB12, its first 6 samples, which share the A0-MC6 uniforms by C-order fill): the selected-outcome reconstruction equals the runtime seed-0 Q and the A0 seed-5 Q; the full 12-sample RB12 reconstruction corresponds to MC12 and is verified by a synthetic test, not on real data; RB6's first-pitch batch has the registered depth-0 composition and RB12 evaluates its first-pitch batch in two chunks (samples 0-5 with exactly the A0-MC6 depth-0 composition, then samples 6-11), so zero first-pitch outcome flips are allowed on the compared first 6 samples (stop on any); continuation batches do not match, so rare continuation outcome flips at CDF boundaries from batch-dependent float rounding are possible (network precision not verified): mismatching decisions and their CDF margins are counted; stop if mismatches exceed 0.1% of decisions or any mismatch has a margin > 1e-5 (judgement values)
